blocks.x: Data & Lakehouse inside Banking & Financial Services: the operating realities we design for, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Banking & Financial Services, data, analytics & lakehouse is the substrate tower: pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture on databricks and snowflake, streaming and event-driven decisioning, executive bi, master data and cataloging, predictive analytics, and data products that generate revenue. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: data engineering & pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture & migration, real-time streaming & event-driven decisioning — delivered on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Fragmented risk and finance data

Credit, market, liquidity and operational risk live in separate estates with divergent reference data. Regulatory reporting leans on manual workarounds, and lineage questions that regulators now ask take expeditions instead of queries.
Fraud and AML decisions too slow

Batch scoring misses the real-time payment window; rules engines generate alert volumes that investigation teams cannot clear. The result is both rising fraud leakage and rising false-positive cost in the same program.
KYC and periodic-review backlog

Customer due diligence refresh cycles lag behind actual risk changes; files queue for weeks in review pools while remediation backlogs grow. Manual file assembly across registries, screening tools and core systems consumes analyst hours that produce no judgment.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: DORA (EU) and DORA (EU). ICT risk, incident reporting, resilience testing and third-party oversight obligations with supervisory scrutiny. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

The weekly rhythm below is identical across programs of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
